content: If there are no clinical features suggestive of monogenic diabetes, evaluate the patient for characteristics indicative of type 2 diabetes and proceed with C-peptide testing. If the C-peptide level is greater than or equal to 200 pmol/L, this finding suggests type 1 diabetes. In such cases, consider conducting additional genetic testing if there is suspicion of monogenic diabetes. If the C-peptide level is less than 200 pmol/L, this result confirms the diagnosis of type 1 diabetes.
